derivation_review: Same-horizon common-currency simple total returns; beginning-wealth risky exposures plus signed cash sum to one. SPD covariance, positive wealth, positive return-variance risk aversion, unrestricted common-rate funding and no costs/nontraded income are explicit.
Common beliefs describe the physical moments for empirical comparison. The directly assumed quadratic mean-variance criterion is not presented as a universal expected-utility representation.

Individual FOC e=gamma Sigma x and negative-definite Hessian establish unique global optimum; exact objective-loss identity verifies strict concavity. Risky weights need not sum to one separately from cash.

Positive wealth-share aggregation and the chosen zero-net-cash economy produce wM=T Sigma^-1 e, T=sum(a/gamma)>0 and lambda=1/T. This justifies positive tangency normalization at equilibrium rather than assuming it at arbitrary prices.

Multiplying the vector price-of-covariance equation by market weights gives the positive market premium and CAPM. The proof is conditional and does not assert general price-existence/uniqueness or a convergent adjustment mechanism.

Cauchy–Schwarz in the SPD covariance inner product proves the CML upper bound under the full zero-population-alpha restriction; equality requires a nonnegative market exposure. The negative-exposure lower ray, all-claims SML and realized-return regression are distinguished. The lab gates its positive-premium CML flag on zero alpha for every available risky claim; arbitrary market/cash combinations retain their computable means and variances without an efficiency claim.

Projection beta/intercept and residual orthogonality are identities; zero population alpha is the additional pricing restriction. Residual variance, covariance versus independence, fixed-weight beta/alpha aggregation and market beta one are explicit.

Positive pricing weights are used only after direct payoff checks; physical probabilities remain distinct. The candidate kernel is not advertised as a valid price rule for arbitrary mean-variance inputs. General SDF/completeness teaching is left to planned c05.

Borrowing constraints introduce a nonnegative multiplier and can change the risky mix. The constrained counterexample proves global optimality and reports failed old-price clearing. Different beliefs, singular covariance and zero market variance identify exact failed proof steps.

The nontraded-income extension adds a portfolio-income covariance vector to individual FOCs and its wealth-weighted aggregate; it is explicitly limited and not a general human-capital pricing theorem.

Population theory, finite-sample OLS, joint model/proxy hypotheses and implementable net investment claims are separated. The selected sample has no empirical significance claim; the research exercise discloses selection and unverified interval assumptions.

resolved_findings.finding: Exercise 3 admitted a positive-alpha security while describing the market/cash benchmark as the actual efficient frontier.
resolved_findings.resolution: Prompt and full solution now call the 12% same-risk combination the conditional CAPM market/cash benchmark. The solution explicitly states that the admitted positive-alpha security invalidates market tangency and that the benchmark is not the true efficient frontier. All numerical answers are preserved.

resolved_findings.finding: The market/cash positive-premium CML flag previously depended only on exposure sign and market premium, so allowed payoff edits with nonzero population alphas could incorrectly imply efficiency.
resolved_findings.resolution: The flag now also requires zero population alpha for every available risky claim. README documents the condition. A targeted admissible A-payoff increase preserves a positive market premium but gives false CML flags, failed clearing and failed candidate pricing consistency; the full baseline output is unchanged.

limitations: Mean-variance preferences, common correct moments, unrestricted equal-rate trading and absent outside income are conditional assumptions, not universal investor descriptions.
The code evaluates a bounded three-claim/four-state candidate-price economy; it is not a price solver, general constrained optimizer or empirical inference system.
The positive pricing checksum is verified for the fixture; arbitrary covariance-based candidate kernels can fail positivity or claim-price identities.
Selected sample coefficients and hypothetical research intervals do not establish statistical validity, market efficiency, mispricing, persistent skill or implementable performance.
